verb:mühen.tx: From Middle High German müejen, müewen, müen, nominalized müeje, müe, from Old High German muoen, nominalized muoī, probably ultimately derived from Proto-West Germanic *mōjan, from Proto-Germanic *mōjaną (“to tire”). Equivalent to Mühe + -en.

noun:Magnat.tx: Borrowed from Late Latin magnātus, derived from magnus (“great”). The historic senses are influenced by Polish magnat, Hungarian mágnás, both from the same Latin word.

verb:mausern.tx: From the noun Mauser (“moulting of feathers”).

verb:maunzen.tx: Nasalised form of mauzen, itself a byform of mauen, from Middle High German māwen.

noun:Molle.tx: Borrowed from Low German, from Middle Low German molle, molde, ultimately from Latin mulctra. Doublet of Mulde, which see.

noun:Mountainbike.tx: Unadapted borrowing from English mountain bike

noun:Mennige.tx: From Middle High German minig, minwe m, from Old High German minio m, from Proto-West Germanic *minnjō (“cinnabar, red lead”).

noun:Morchel.tx: From Middle High German morchel, morhel, from Old High German morhila, morahila (“more, carrot, parsnip”), diminutive of Old High German moraha (“tree-root, plant root”).

noun:Minderwertigkeitsgefühl.tx: Coined by Austrian psychotherapist Alfred Adler, Minderwertigkeit + -s- + Gefühl.

noun:Mantille.tx: Borrowed from Spanish mantilla or French mantille.

noun:Meinungsäußerung.tx: From Meinung + -s- + Äußerung. Compare Dutch meningsuiting.

noun:Maschinist.tx: Borrowed from French machiniste. By surface analysis, Maschine + -ist.

noun:Muskete.tx: Borrowed from French mousquet, from Italian moschetto.

noun:Matrize.tx: Borrowed from French matrice. Doublet of Matrix.

noun:Massel.tx: Borrowed from Yiddish מזל (mazel, “luck, destiny”), from medieval Hebrew מַזָּל (mazzāl). Related to vermasseln.

noun:Misthaufen.tx: From Middle High German misthoufe. Equivalent to Mist + Haufen. Compare Dutch mesthoop.

phrase:mein Vater erklärt mir jeden Sonn.tx: Literally, “my father explains our nine planets to me every Sunday”.

noun:Metze.tx: From a regional variant of Mechthild, perhaps influenced by Magd.

noun:Maische.tx: Alteration of older Maisch, from Middle High German meisch (“mash”), from Old High German *meisk, from Proto-West Germanic *maisk, from Proto-Germanic *maiskaz, from Proto-Indo-European *moiḱ-sḱ-o/eh₂-, from *meyḱ- (“mix”). Cognate with English mash. The spelling with -ai- is of Upper German origin. It is unusual insofar as modern ai-spellings in Germanic words are otherwise influenced by related …

phrase:mein Vater erklärt mir jeden Sonn.tx: Literally, “my father explains our night sky to me every Sunday”.

pt: mint (place for producing coins); money, coin, coinage
verb:münzen.tx: From Münze (“mint (place for producing coins); money, coin, coinage”) + -en (verb-forming suffix).

noun:Maar.tx: Attested since at least the 16th century, from an underlying Middle High German *mar(e). Adopted into scientific parlance during the 19th century from Central Franconian dialects of the Eifel region, home to many maars, which often include the word in their names. The Central Franconian term also has the broader sense of “pool, cesspit, swamp”, which touches on Middle High German muor (“bog”) or …

noun:Mutterkorn.tx: Mutter + Korn, associated in folk etymology with Gebärmutter, from its therapeutic use in gynecology.

noun:Megäre.tx: Learned borrowing from Latin Megaera, from Ancient Greek Μέγαιρα (Mégaira), from μεγαίρω (megaírō, “to grudge, to envy”). For the usage as a common noun, cf. German mégère, Italian megera and Russian меге́ра (megéra).

noun:Methusalem.tx: Borrowed from Hebrew מְתוּשֶׁלַח (M'tušelaḥ), also spelled מְתוּשָׁלַח (M'tušalaḥ).

verb:mucken.tx: 15th century, from a Proto-West Germanic verb, probably attested in Old High German firmucken (“to be obtuse”). Cognate with Middle Low German mucken, Dutch mokken.

noun:Marineinfanterist.tx: From Marineinfanterie + -ist, equivalent to Marine + Infanterist.

noun:Mimik.tx: From Latin mīmicus, from Ancient Greek μῑμικός (mīmikós, “belonging to mimes”), from μῖμος (mîmos, “imitator, actor”); attested since 18th century.

noun:Mitleidenschaft.tx: From mitleiden (“to feel compassion”) + -schaft (“-ship”) or Mitleid (“compassion”) + -en- + -schaft.

noun:Muli.tx: 19th century, from an Alemannic German or Austro-Bavarian dialect. Possibly from an inherited form of Middle High German mūl + the diminutive suffix -li. Alternatively from Italian mulo with its plural muli associated with that suffix. Ultimately from Latin mulus, whence also Maultier.

noun:Maloche.tx: 18th century, via Rotwelsch (thieves’ cant) from Yiddish מלאָכה (melokhe, “work, labour”), from Hebrew מְלָאכָה (məlāḵā́, “work, labour”).

noun:Monotonie.tx: Borrowed from French monotonie. By surface analysis, monoton (“monotonous”) + -ie (abstract noun suffix).

noun:Mundvoll.tx: From Middle High German muntvol, from Old High German mundfol, from Proto-West Germanic *munþafull, equivalent to Mund + -voll.

noun:Mythomanie.tx: From Mythos + -manie. See also English mythomania, French mythomanie.

verb:modulieren.tx: From Latin modulāri + -ieren, from Latin modulus, from Latin modus

noun:Musikvideo.tx: From Musik + Video, borrowed from English music video.

phrase:Marsch durch die Institutionen.tx: Literally, “[the] march through the institutions”, coined by German activist Rudi Dutschke in 1967.

noun:Meniskus.tx: 18th century, learned borrowing from Ancient Greek μηνίσκος (mēnískos).

noun:Midlife-Crisis.tx: Unadapted borrowing from English mid-life crisis.

noun:Messwein.tx: From Mess + Wein. Compare Dutch miswijn.

noun:Musselin.tx: Borrowed from French mousseline, from Italian mussolina, from Mussolo (“Mosul”). First attested in the 18th century.

noun:Märchenwald.tx: From Märchen (“fairy tale, folk tale”) + Wald (“forest”).

o: mein Englisch ist nicht das Gelbe vom Ei
phrase:my English is not the yellow from.tx: Hyperliteral translation (Denglisch) of German mein Englisch ist nicht das Gelbe vom Ei, aber es geht (“my English is not the best, but it's alright”).

noun:Marienbad.tx: From Marie + -n- + Bad, a calque of Latin balneum Mariae.

noun:Mariendistel.tx: From Marien- (combining form of Maria) + Distel (“thistle”).

noun:Mobilheim.tx: From mobil + Heim. Calque of English mobile home.

noun:Maschinenbauer.tx: By surface analysis, Maschine (“machine”) + -n + Bauer (“builder”), or, by surface analysis, Maschinenbau (“machine building”) + -er (“agent”).

phrase:mehr Glück als Verstand.tx: Literally, “more luck than wit”. Compare Dutch meer geluk dan wijsheid.

noun:Metrum.tx: Borrowed from Latin metrum, derived from Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron). Doublet of Meter.

noun:Matchball.tx: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from match ball. Compare Czech mečbol, Norwegian Bokmål matchball, Polish meczbol, and Slovak mečbal.

noun:Mittelgewicht.tx: Calque of English middleweight. By surface analysis, mittel- + Gewicht.

noun:Makramee.tx: Borrowed from French macramé, from Italian macramè.

noun:Mief.tx: Spread since around 1900 from Berlin. Probably a phonetic variant of earlier Muff (“stench, mouldy smell, mustiness, mold”).

noun:Mobber.tx: Borrowed from English mobber, equivalent to mobben + -er.
